# TDPdf v1.20.0.0

A fork-sync release pulling the useful features and fixes from upstream [**SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF**](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF) (v1.7.0 and v1.7.1) and adapting them to TDPdf's diverged multi-tab architecture. This build ships everything merged to `main` since the last release, headlined by the changes below. See [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the complete per-version history.

As always: this fork only exists because upstream KillerPDF is a genuinely great, dark-themed, no-telemetry, no-cloud Windows PDF editor. **Go star [the upstream project](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF).**

Upstream's v1.7.0 was mostly an internal refactor — about 8,700 lines moved into a new viewer control to enable split-pane — which doesn't apply to this fork. What did come across is the substantial set of correctness fixes riding alongside it, and they turned out to matter more here than upstream. Porting also surfaced four TDPdf-specific bugs of our own.

## Highlights

### The annotations your PDF already has now actually show up
Sticky notes, highlights, stamps, ink made in another app, filled form values — they were in the file and simply never painted. PDFium doesn't draw annotation appearance streams unless asked, and we never asked.

This went well past the screen. **Save Flattened and Export as Images build a new document out of the pixels, so anything the source carried was silently dropped from the output, and printing left it out too.**

Fixing it properly meant taking over from the PDF library: its annotation-aware path tears down a form-fill environment while the page is still open, which corrupts PDFium and crashes on a *later* call. TDPdf now owns that lifetime itself. Deliberately left off for OCR (a reviewer's sticky note isn't page content) and for sidebar thumbnails (they render every page on open, and the cost isn't worth markup you can't read at 256px).

### 100% finally means 100%
Outside Continuous view, asking for 100% actually rendered at roughly **137% on A4 and 145% on US Letter** — and the percentage readout, the zoom dropdown and the zoom limits were all wrong along with it.

Zoom now means true zoom everywhere: **Ctrl+0**, **Ctrl+1**, every preset, the wheel, the readout and the 5–400% range agree in Single, Two-Page, Grid and Continuous alike.

> Two side effects worth knowing: memory at maximum zoom roughly halves, and a very small page can no longer fit-to-width past 400% — which is how Continuous already behaved.

### Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Thai and Arabic survive the save
Type non-Latin text into an annotation, and it looked right on screen — then saved as a row of empty boxes, silently.

Two reasons. The font resolver only ever looked at `.ttf` files, and nearly every CJK face on Windows ships as a `.ttc` collection (Yu Gothic, MS Gothic, Meiryo, YaHei, JhengHei), so those fonts were never even found. And nothing checked whether the chosen font could draw the characters at all.

TDPdf now reads collection fonts and picks a face by real glyph coverage, preferring what Windows itself falls back to — while always keeping your own font when it covers the text. If nothing installed can draw a character, you're told **as you place the text**, with the characters listed, instead of finding out after saving and reopening.

### Perspective correction
Photographed a page at an angle? Turn on perspective correction in Transform, drag the four corner handles onto the page outline, and Apply straightens it into a true rectangle — composed with rotation, deskew, scaling and flipping in one pass.

Transform's settings are collapsible sections now, so everything still fits.

> Single-page only, on purpose: the corner outline is traced against *one* page's edges, and applying that same quad to a whole selection would warp the others by an outline that was never theirs.

### Night mode that spares your pictures
Photos and figures keep their real colors while the page around them goes dark. Right-click the moon (or press **Shift+N**) for **Invert images too** — which is what makes a *scanned* document, where the whole page is one image, readable in night mode.

**Ctrl+I** still toggles night mode.

### Shortcuts that work on your keyboard
Punctuation shortcuts were matched by key *position* — a US-layout assumption. On a German keyboard "?" is Shift+ß and "=" is Shift+0, so **Ctrl+?** and **Ctrl+=** pressed keys the app wasn't listening for. They now match the character your layout actually types, and the menus show the right spelling.

**Ctrl+?** never worked at all, on any layout — that's fixed too. **Ctrl+NumPad0** joins Ctrl+0 as a zoom reset for layouts where the digit needs Shift.

### Smaller things
- **Ctrl+Shift+W** closes every tab but the current one; tabs get a right-click menu.
- **Fit Width / Fit Page are remembered** across launches, so small screens stop re-picking it every time.
- **Page-number tooltips** on every page in every view mode.
- The **shortcuts list** uses the window width instead of a cramped fixed card.
- The **app-size readout** stops parking itself on the status bar.
- **"Confirm before opening links"** now has a Settings checkbox — ticking "don't ask again" used to be a one-way trapdoor with no way back.

## Fixes worth calling out

- **Annotations on a rotated page saved in the wrong place.** The save path never read page rotation, so anything on a quarter-turned page landed a quarter turn out of position and scaled on swapped axes.
- **A filled form you saved could be destroyed when you reopened it.** The form appearance streams were missing a required length field, and a cold open could fall through to raster recovery — flattening your filled form into flat images. Multiline fields ran together on one line, and curly quotes, dashes and bullets turned into `?`.
- **A signature dropped on a form field was invisible**, hidden behind the field's own overlay.
- **Clicking a page could crash** with `'∞' is not a valid value for property 'Height'` — and the source was a bad saved signature size that got written *onto* the annotation, so it crashed every render afterwards.
- **Editing bold or italic text made it regular.** `Helvetica-BoldOblique` was being mangled into a font name that resolves nowhere, so the editor quietly fell back to the default font.
- **Owner-restricted PDFs with a malformed structure wouldn't open at all** — the retry threw from inside its own error handler, so the recovery path never ran.
- **The eyedropper's OK could be silently thrown away**, leaving the tool drawing the previous color.
- **Cropping a rotated page cropped the wrong region.** *(Ours, found while porting.)*
- **Fit Page did nothing in Continuous view.** *(Ours, found while porting.)*

## Notes

**Not ported:** split-pane and the viewer-control refactor it's built on, the shared "Killer Tools family" file dialogs, the family card theming / new app icon / themed system menu, the Settings-panel-into-flyouts rework, the toolbar appearance menu, the sidebar side swap, and all localization — TDPdf is English-only. The `killerpdf://` protocol handler was skipped as branding-bound scaffolding for a browser extension we don't ship. Upstream's machine-wide PDF registration fix doesn't apply: TDPdf's installer is already scope-aware, because it has to support Intune.

**Verified rather than assumed:** upstream's rotated-page transform fix and odd/even print fix were already correct here — TDPdf fixed both independently in v1.19.0.0.

**Needs Windows testing.** This release changes the render pipeline, save geometry, zoom in every view mode and the font resolver, none of which can be exercised on the macOS build machine. If you hit something, please [open an issue](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/issues).
